{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The lighthouse on Vardnes had been automated the spring Margit turned seventy, and the men from the maritime authority had come with clipboards and a padlock and the careful courtesy of people dismantling someone's life. She had made them coffee. It seemed the thing to do.

They left her the keeper's cottage, which was hers anyway, and the path down to the landing, which belonged to nobody. The lamp still turned. That was the part she had not expected: that it would go on sweeping the strait every eleven seconds without her, as though she had only ever been a guest in its routine.

She kept the logbook out of habit. Wind, visibility, vessels sighted. Some weeks the vessels column stayed empty and she wrote the date anyway, in the same square hand her husband had taught her, because a gap in the record looked like a gap in attention and she did not intend to be caught inattentive.

Her son telephoned on Sundays from Bodø. He asked about her hip and the roof and whether she had thought about the flat near his family. She said the hip was fine, the roof was fine, and the flat had a view of a car park. He laughed, which meant he had stopped expecting a different answer.

At dusk she climbed the tower stairs and stood beneath the lens as it began its circuit. The light did not need her. She understood that. But it had never once, in forty years, turned without her watching, and she saw no reason to start now."}
